NO. 003 · Songbirds & City Birds / Columbidae · Pigeons & Doves

Spotted Dove

珠颈斑鸠 · zhū jǐng bān jiū Spilopelia chinensis
Resident Abundant 28–32 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A 'wild pigeon' wearing a collar of pearls

Often mistaken for a pigeon, but the black collar scattered with white dots settles it at once. The Spotted Dove walks with a nodding head and clatters loudly into flight — the most everyday sound of any housing estate in the Pearl River Delta.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • NeckA broad black patch from the sides of the neck to the nape, densely spotted white — the single most reliable mark.
  • ColourHead grey-brown; back and wings pinkish brown with pale fringes giving a scaly look; underparts pale pink-buff; long tail with large white tips to the outer feathers.
  • ShapePlump, small-headed and long-tailed; bill slender and short with a soft base; legs purplish red.
  • FlightLoud wing-claps on take-off and landing, a bounding flight, and conspicuous white tail tips when the tail is fanned.

Behaviour

Feeds mostly by walking on the ground, taking grass seed, fallen fruit and human food debris; flushes almost vertically when startled. Usually in pairs or small parties, tolerant and thoroughly adapted to dense city. The nest is perfunctory — a platform of a few twigs — and it will lay on air-conditioner units, windowsills and flower pots, which is why it so often ends up living in the same building as we do.

Voice

Field recording

Recording Manoj Karingamadathil / xeno-canto XC495643 · Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 · Original file

A three-note 'coo-coo-coo', the last note drawn out and falling, repeated for long stretches — one of the most soporific sounds of a southern afternoon. Courting males add a low rolling growl while bowing and spreading the tail.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • almost any estate lawn
  • Seaside Park lawns
  • Jinwan field margins
  • Tangjiawan Old Town
Field note
Don't call it a pigeon too quickly: feral pigeons are stockier and have unspotted necks. A pearl collar means Spotted Dove.
